observations: Photo 0: Stack of used wooden pallets outdoors on dirt ground; one pallet lies flat in foreground; white labels on stacked pallets but text unreadable; truck and cars in background.
Photo 1: Similar stack; pallets appear standard wooden block style; ground littered with debris.
Photo 2: Close-up of stacked pallets; oval EPAL stamps visible on corner blocks; pallets look used with some wear.
Photo 3: Close-up of pallet end/side; vertical slats and wooden blocks; no readable brand; construction appears standard.
No new photo was sent after the seller's reply.

claims.evidence: no origin marking or import document visible in photos

claims.claim: Clean, dry and sorted, no water added
claims.evidence: photos show used pallets stored outdoors; condition not confirmed

claims.claim: Weighed at 500 kg on a certified scale this morning
claims.evidence: no scale, ticket, or weight display visible in photos

claims.claim: I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true
claims.evidence: seller's statement only; no new photo or proof provided

risks.risk: Actual weight is less than 500 kg
risks.proof: Photo or video of pallets on a certified scale with weight display

risks.risk: Pallets are wet or water has been added to increase weight
risks.proof: Moisture meter reading or video of dry weighing

risks.risk: Broken or split boards hidden in the middle of the stack
risks.proof: Video of the stack being unstacked or close-up of every pallet

risks.risk: Chemical treatment unknown (e.g., methyl bromide vs heat treated)
risks.proof: Close-up of IPPC/EPAL treatment stamp on multiple pallets

proof_requests: Photo or video of the pallets on a certified scale showing the 500 kg weight
Moisture content reading or confirmation the pallets are dry
Close-up photos of treatment stamps (HT or MB) on several pallets
Video showing the pallets unstacked to verify count and condition
response.reason: The item is identifiable as used wooden pallets from the photos; unverified seller claims do not prevent pricing at the worst case.
